source: For every lens in data/lenses.json: who it is for and who it is not for, one sentence each with no hedging word, and the rule's source as show, book or author with a URL. Lane 2, section 4 (L-4).
confidenceNote: Copy, not figures. The pair is the advice translator from the master prompt section 5; a lens without both does not ship.
note: Generated by tests/tools/build-lenses-copy.js from data/lenses.json; the sentences there are the master build's (D-175), four rewritten here to drop a hedging word. lenses.name: FAT and wants
lenses.plain: Needs inside half of take-home
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with take-home pay and the three needs lines filled in.
lenses.notForWhom: Between jobs, with no take-home to divide: read the runway instead.

lenses.plain: A fifth of take-home saved
lenses.forWhom: Someone starting out who wants three numbers and no spreadsheet.
lenses.notForWhom: High earners in expensive cities: rent alone breaks the 50 for needs, and the 20 is too little.

lenses.name: Money Guy 25%
lenses.plain: Save a quarter of what you earn
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a job and no high-interest debt.
lenses.notForWhom: Carrying credit card debt: clear it first, this comes later.

source.title: The Money Guy Show
source.author: Brian Preston and Bo Hanson
source.where: The Financial Order of Operations; the 25% rule; the 20/3/8 car rule; the rate-by-age debt rule

lenses.name: Conscious spending
lenses.plain: One rich-life line, ruthless on the rest
lenses.forWhom: Someone who hates budgets and wants one line to protect.
lenses.notForWhom: A month that does not close: the ruthless part comes before the guilt-free part.

lenses.name: Your Money or Your Life
lenses.plain: A month of spending, in hours of your life
lenses.forWhom: Anyone who has filled in Real Hourly Wage and wonders whether a line is worth it.
lenses.notForWhom: Retired or between jobs: with no wage there are no hours to price in.

source.title: Your Money or Your Life
source.author: Vicki Robin and Joe Dominguez
source.where: Step 2, your real hourly wage; step 3, life energy per purchase

lenses.name: Die With Zero
lenses.plain: Spend when you can use it
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a date of birth entered and a fear of dying rich.
lenses.notForWhom: A household with no cushion yet: the book assumes the basics are covered before the spending curve starts.

source.title: Die With Zero
source.author: Bill Perkins
source.where: Rule 8, the peak net worth date; rule 3, spend on experiences by age

lenses.name: Avalanche
lenses.plain: Highest rate first
lenses.forWhom: Anyone who can keep paying a plan without seeing a balance disappear.
lenses.notForWhom: Someone who needs an early win to keep going: see the snowball.

lenses.name: Snowball
lenses.plain: Smallest balance first
lenses.forWhom: Someone with several debts who needs one gone to believe the rest can go.
lenses.notForWhom: One big debt at a high rate: there is nothing to snowball; see the avalanche.

lenses.plain: Pay it off or invest, by your decade

lenses.notForWhom: Credit card debt at any age: that is always above the line.

lenses.notForWhom: Someone without an emergency fund: neither wins until the cushion exists.

lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a yearly bill that lands all at once: insurance, a gift season, a registration.
